correctness.rationale: With J^2=0, every unit uniquely splits as a diagonal torus times an additive unipotent radical. For fixed active-arrow support S, the explicit coadjoint action shifts diagonal functionals in the incidence-column subspace of dimension n-c(S). Its quotient has q^{c(S)} cosets. The diagonal torus has (q-1)^{r(S)}-element weight orbits, and hence (q-1)^{|S|-r(S)} such orbits, with loops counted as incidence-zero edges. Their products give the exact number and cardinality of each coadjoint orbit. A second weighted count recovers all q^{n+|E|} dual points; the Tutte identity is a direct substitution in its rank expansion. Explicit independent orbit enumeration over F2,F3,F4, and deletion-contraction comparisons for several field orders, all passed. Boundary cases include empty graphs, loops, parallel arrows and disconnected quivers.

value.rationale: For a natural all-quiver family of finite-dimensional algebras, the theorem determines every orbit size and its multiplicity for the coadjoint action of the full unit group, an intrinsic group/Lie-algebra invariant. It establishes orientation independence and identifies the entire distribution with a graphic Tutte specialization for arbitrary loops, parallel arrows and finite-field characteristics. These are structural nontrivial conclusions beyond a minimum-index bound or isolated finite census, with direct examples for forests and cycles.
